question: When is the best time for a midwife to do the initial physical check for visible birth defects?

options.A: Immediately after making sure the newborn is breathing and stable
options.B: Twenty-four hours after delivery during the routine pediatric review
options.C: Only after the baby has completed the first successful breastfeed
options.D: When the mother is discharged home from the postnatal ward

explanation: Airway and breathing stabilization always come first. The structural check happens right after during the normal transition period to catch major defects early. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do midwives routinely check the anal opening during the newborn's first assessment?

options.A: To prevent the development of neonatal jaundice
options.B: To measure the baby's core body temperature accurately
options.C: To detect conditions like imperforate anus early
options.D: To stimulate the first meconium passage

explanation: Checking the anal opening helps identify lower intestinal malformations such as imperforate anus before feeding begins. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the best position for a newborn with an open spinal defect (myelomeningocele) during care?

options.A: Flat on the back flat against the mattress
options.B: Upright in a seated infant carrier

explanation: Placing the baby on its stomach or side prevents direct pressure and injury to the delicate exposed spinal tissues. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h2)

question: A newborn has a congenital diaphragmatic hernia and needs breathing support. Which method should the midwife avoid if possible?
explanation: Bag-valve-mask ventilation pushes air into the stomach and intestines, which worsens lung compression inside the chest cavity when a diaphragmatic hernia is present. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h2)

question: What material is best used to cover an exposed bowel in a newborn with gastroschisis before transfer?

options.A: A thick layer of zinc oxide ointment and bandages
options.B: Warm sterile saline-soaked gauze and a protective wrap
options.C: Dry cotton wool pads soaked in methylated spirit
options.D: An adhesive plaster pulled tight across the abdomen

explanation: Moist, warm sterile coverings prevent the delicate exposed bowel loops from drying out and getting infected. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is preventing a drop in body temperature especially critical for a newborn with major structural defects?

options.A: Low body temperature causes immediate closure of congenital heart defects
options.B: Hypothermia stops the kidneys from producing urine completely
options.C: Cold skin prevents effective surgical repair later in the week
options.D: Cold stress worsens metabolic acidosis and increases mortality risk

explanation: Newborns with surgical conditions handle cold poorly. Hypothermia quickly triggers metabolic complications that worsen their clinical condition. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h3)

question: How should a midwife approach parents immediately after finding a birth defect in their newborn?

options.A: At the busy nurse's station while charting routine vitals
options.B: By telephone before the father is allowed into the maternity unit
options.C: In a private space using simple language and deep empathy
options.D: With detailed medical statistics about rare chromosomal disorders

explanation: Private settings and clear, gentle communication help parents process difficult news and build trust in the healthcare team. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is an appropriate reassurance for parents grieving a newborn with a birth defect?

options.A: Suggest that the condition will resolve on its own without treatment
options.B: Blame traditional herbal remedies taken during the first trimester
options.C: Explain that anomalies are common and usually not caused by their actions
options.D: Promise that modern surgery will make the baby completely normal

explanation: Relieving parental guilt is an essential part of psychological support, as many parents wrongfully blame themselves for birth defects. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h4)

question: What key document must go with a newborn being transferred to a bigger hospital for birth defect care?

options.A: A signed consent form for immediate major surgery
options.B: A receipt showing full payment of hospital admission fees
options.C: A detailed and legible referral letter with clinical findings
options.D: The birth mother's national identity card and marriage certificate

explanation: Receiving doctors and nurses need clear documentation of the baby's condition and treatments already given to continue care without delay. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h5)

question: A midwife at a primary health clinic has stabilized a newborn with a large omphalocele. What is the next critical action before ambulance transport?

options.A: Discharge the mother so she can travel in a separate taxi behind
options.B: Wait until the newborn passes its first meconium stool naturally
options.C: Administer a full course of therapeutic oral antibiotics
options.D: Ensure IV access, thermal protection, and accompanying trained staff

explanation: Safe transport requires preparations before travel, including fluids, warmth, and monitoring personnel to manage any changes on the road. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T8#BMP220_U2_T8_h5)
